finding: ONE CONFIRMATORY REPEAT IS NOT A RUNAWAY LOOP
the_defect: _tool_loop_closure closed the moment EVERY call in a round repeated one already made. Rounds 22, 24 and 25 each measured real dense anatomy, re-read the ledger to CONFIRM it -- a correct verification instinct -- and that confirmation ended the loop before they could write. All three closed with observations still in budget.

the_contract_now.one_all_repeat_round: CONTINUE. The round may be confirming.
the_contract_now.two_consecutive: CLOSE. That is a no-progress cycle, and runaway protection is what the rule was for.
the_contract_now.any_fresh_call: RESETS the counter. It counts a CYCLE, not the total confirmations a round made.
the_contract_now.above_it: the observation budget and the failure tolerance are unchanged and still outrank it.

why_not_simply_remove_it: [S010 11] the bounded repeat mechanism existed for a reason and removing it would permit infinite repeated calls. The distinction that matters is ONE CONFIRMATORY REPEAT versus a REPEATED NO-PROGRESS LOOP, and consecutive-ness is the progress evidence.

verification.red_before_green: the test failed with TypeError -- repeat_rounds did not exist
verification.call_site_and_reset_asserted: the test greps engine.py for repeat_rounds=repeat_rounds AND for the reset. A counter that never resets turns the second confirmation of a long round into loop death even when fresh work happened in between -- the same defect, slower.
mutations: closure never fires -> two-in-a-row case FAILS (runaway unbounded)
closure fires on the first repeat -> the confirmation case FAILS
counter never resets -> the reset assertion FAILS

a_test_encoded_the_OLD_contract: hcli/test_tool_observation_budget.py::test_the_failure_closers_are_untouched asserted that a single all-repeat round closes the loop. That is precisely the semantics S010 10 changes, so the assertion was updated to the new contract -- one repeat continues, two consecutive close, and the budget still outranks both -- with the reason written beside it. Recorded as a deliberate steered change, not a test quietly bent to fit.
the_baseline_is_not_a_stable_number: two runs of the SAME baseline commit reported 65 and then 64. At least one failure is non-deterministic. That matters for every future delta claim and it weakens 'return to zero' as a target: the honest form is the INTRODUCED-BY-HEAD set, which is empty, rather than a count that moves on its own.
scar: A LEGITIMATE VERIFICATION INSTINCT WAS EQUIVALENT TO LOOP DEATH.
